# Untying Prefill and Decode Loops in Looped Language Models

> Looped (recurrent-depth) language models run one block of layers several times per token and, at inference, run the
> same number of loops to prefill the prompt and to decode each answer token. This work unties the two with a small
> loop adapter (LoRA + per-loop RoPE-commuting KV maps on a frozen model; one set of parameters for all 16 pairs of
> prefill loops m and decode loops n up to four) and measures what each count buys on Ouro-2.6B, Ouro-1.4B,
> Ouro-2.6B-Thinking, Ouro-1.4B-Thinking, SenseNova-Loop-9B-Preview and Lev looped decision models. Every number in the
> paper is recomputed from released per-item scores by ouro/scripts/paper_numbers.py.

Main findings (95% paired bootstrap intervals in the paper):
- Prefill loops mainly buy knowledge and long-context accuracy; decode loops mainly buy multi-step math (on the tested
  benchmarks; task- and prompt-dependent). Ouro-2.6B, one decode loop, prefill 4 vs prefill 1 within one adapter:
  MMLU +15.2, RULER-16K +8.6.
- Prefill 4 / decode 2 on Ouro-2.6B-Thinking scores at least as high as native 2/2 on all eight benchmarks tested
  (significantly higher on five) and within two points of native 4/4 on six; it answers GSM8K in 0.55x the time of
  native 4/4 (batch 1, prefill included) and is 1.0 point below it on all 1,319 problems (93.3 vs 94.2).
- With the same adapter at prefill 2 / decode 2 as control, the prefill loops account for the MMLU-Pro (+8.1) and
  HELMET (+7.5) gains over native 2/2, not for GSM8K, MATH-500 or MBPP+.
- Lev looped decision models prefilled with more loops are 4.4-7.5 points more accurate at one decision loop on three
  backbones (LevBench public development set), across four seeds and against a control trained twice as long.
- A per-frequency complex key scale commutes with RoPE, so one stored prompt KV cache serves every decode loop exactly
  (512/512 greedy tokens identical).

Limitations stated by the author: more prefill loops hurt few-shot MATH, short-context retrieval and (1.4B) 3-shot BBH;
at three or more decode loops one prompt KV cache trails the native model on retrieval; more prefill loops raise time to
first token; gains against native models include training the adapter; the 1.4B adapters lose 3-shot BBH.
